transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-04-06
Time: 16:30 UTC (09:30 PT)
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Carlos Ortega (Redwood SE), Leah Park (Redwood SE), Priya Rao (NexaHead ML), Tom Briggs (Platform), Sara Linton (CTO), Devon Hale (SRE)

Auto-summary: quick recap of stress test, alignment on stricter pin windows and an emergency swap drill. Agreed deliverables.

[00:00] Maya Chen: Hi everyone, thanks for joining, quick check on audio then we'll jump in. Hey Priya, can you see the deck?
[00:06] Priya Rao: Yep can see, loud and clear, thanks.
[00:10] Maya Chen: Cool. So agenda, quick results from the 48 hour stress run, go over the model pin approach we suggested last week, then the emergency swap drill and next steps. Carlos will take the deep bits.
[00:22] Carlos Ortega: Hey all. Quick note, we ran pinned variant A (a redwood-ggml-quant-ish) and fallback to B on error, and the stress test hit the warm KV cache eviction corner twice, so we saw a bump in tail latency. I know some of the names in the transcript get munged but the thing to watch is the long tail when the prefix cache gets evicted.
[00:45] Tom Briggs: Can you quantify the bump? I saw a spike in our metrics last night around 03:12 UTC.
[00:52] Carlos Ortega: Right, we have a 95th percentile baseline of 180ms for the pinned path, fallback path was 420ms, but during cache eviction events the pinned path transiently jumped to ~1.2s. That's the scenario we're worried about for user facing flows.
[01:10] Priya Rao: Ok, that 1.2s is not acceptable for our chat real-time UIs, so we need a hard SLA for tail or an automatic soft-fallback earlier.
[01:20] Leah Park: We proposed a soft-fallback threshold where if token latency exceeds X ms for three consecutive calls the router shifts to the fallback variant for that session. That reduces the chance of user seeing intermittent 1s spikes.
[01:35] Sara Linton: Are we talking about switching mid-conversation? That could change generation tone. Concern about semantic drift.
[01:43] Carlos Ortega: Good point. The soft-fallback preserves KV cache as possible by doing a shadow call to fallback in parallel for a small sample, then we compare output quality using a delta heuristic. If the fallback matches quality thresholds we switch. It's not perfect but reduces user-visible slowness.
[02:05] Devon Hale: On the automation, our staging environment couldn't reproduce the eviction pattern; looks like the production seq length distro is different. I can try to replay the exact token lengths from the logs.
[02:18] Tom Briggs: Also want to raise data residency and audit requirements - when we do emergency swaps, the fallback variant must still observe the same logging and KMS behavior.
[02:30] Maya Chen: Absolutely, those are in the runbook. Carlos, can you walk through the emergency swap steps you want to test in the tabletop?
[02:36] Carlos Ortega: Sure. Current emergency swap flow we suggested: 1) Detect sustained tail latency above threshold, 2) mark affected routes as "swap-candidate", 3) trigger a shadow cutover for 2% of traffic, 4) validate correctness and observability, 5) if success gradually ramp to 100% with canary timers, else rollback. For the drill we want to exercise the manual cutover too, i.e., operator-initiated swap via the console.
[03:05] Priya Rao: The step 3 shadow cutover — do we have enough telemetry to compare outputs automatically? We don't want to have to do manual QA for every swap.
[03:16] Carlos Ortega: We have token-level deltas, embedding similarity checks, and a quick n-gram overlap signal. But for clinical phrasing we recommend a short eval set run as a sanity check; that can be automated in the pipeline.
[03:31] Tom Briggs: Is there any risk the shadow calls will double cost? Our budget is tight for the POC.
[03:36] Leah Park: The shadow percentage is small (2%) and the platform supports budget caps. Also shadow calls can be sampled to limit cost. We included a cost estimate in the appendix.
[03:48] Sara Linton: I remember last week you mentioned pin window — length of time a model remains pinned after selection. What is the suggestion now?
[03:56] Carlos Ortega: Based on the stress runs, we're recommending a shorter pin window for variant A — 15 minutes — with automatic re-eval on traffic patterns. Previously we had 1 hour. Shorter window reduces exposure to stale cache effects.
[04:10] Priya Rao: That feels aggressive, any chance of thrash where we keep flipping models for the same session?
[04:16] Carlos Ortega: We guard against thrash with session stickiness and a cool-down for the session of 10 minutes after a switch. So you can only switch once per 10 minute window.
[04:28] Devon Hale: For the emergency swap drill could we simulate cache eviction by forcing KV cache clear on the instance? Might be the fastest way to reproduce.
[04:36] Carlos Ortega: Yes, we can simulate with the --evict-kv flag in the staging harness. We'll include the exact command in the runbook.
[04:45] Priya Rao: One operational question — how do we handle audit logs and SSO during an operator-initiated swap? We need traceability.
[04:53] Maya Chen: The console integrates with your SAML SSO and every operator action emits an audit event to your logging endpoint. We'll add an explicit checklist item in the runbook.
[05:02] Tom Briggs: On semantic drift, do you have a rollback heuristic? If the fallback starts producing hallucinations or shifts policy, we need an escape hatch.
[05:11] Leah Park: The escape hatch is twofold: automatic quality regression monitoring using eval prompts and a manual quick rollback that re-enables the previous pin. Also you can pin a frozen model version to an edge route to prevent further changes.
[05:26] Priya Rao: Can that frozen pin be enforced at the platform level so our product team can't accidentally unpin?
[05:31] Carlos Ortega: Yes, roles and RBAC can restrict who can change pin state; we can add a label to block changes without a two-person approval.
[05:40] Sara Linton: Ok, seems reasonable. I'd like to focus the drill on two scenarios: 1) automated detection and soft-fallback succeeding, 2) manual operator swap because of a cross-region outage.
[05:51] Maya Chen: Great, so deliverables are the updated runbook, the pinned vs fallback latency spreadsheet, and scheduling the tabletop. Any other blockers?
[05:59] Priya Rao: For the latency spreadsheet, can you include percentile deltas for 50/95/99 and a breakdown by sequence-length bucket? That will help us size the user impact.
[06:09] Carlos Ortega: Yes, we'll include buckets (<=64, 65-256, 256+). We'll also mark which runs had KV eviction simulated.
[06:18] Devon Hale: On the staging tests, I'll also try to replay the exact sequence length distribution and report back. If I can't recreate it I'll share a trace for Redwood to replay in their harness.
[06:28] Maya Chen: Perfect. Quick note on cost — Leah, any modeling for worst-case cost during a swap?
[06:33] Leah Park: Worst case if you do a 100% simultaneous swap you could see a short-term doubling for those routes but with our canary timers it's gradual. For budgeting we suggest a ramp schedule with a hard budget cap to auto-stop the swap if cost exceeds X% of baseline. We'll define X in the runbook.
[06:50] Tom Briggs: Can that budget cap be per-route? We don't want a single high-volume route to throttle everything.
[06:55] Carlos Ortega: Yes, per-route and per-tenant caps are supported.
[07:02] Maya Chen: Alright, last part — timeline and next steps recap. Maya to share latency CSV by Friday, Carlos to update runbook, Devon to run staging test, Redwood to schedule tabletop for Tuesday 4/13. Also we will include a short checklist for SSO/audit verification.
[07:20] Priya Rao: Sounds good. One small ask — can you include a short 'decision matrix' for when to prefer dedicated vs hosted fallback? Our security folks want guidance.
[07:29] Maya Chen: We'll add a decision matrix, yes. It will list tradeoffs: latency, cost, data residency, SLA.
[07:36] Sara Linton: Ok if we can get those artifacts this week we can run the drill next week. Thanks everyone.
[07:42] Maya Chen: Thanks all. We'll follow up in email with links.

End of transcript.

Notes about transcription quality: Some proper nouns may be slightly off (e.g., 'KV cache' sometimes transcribed as 'K-V cash' or 'prefix cache' as 'pre-fix cache'). There were a few overlaps and quick crosstalk sections.

Recap (at 07:36):
- Redwood (Maya/Carlos/Leah) to deliver: pinned-vs-fallback latency CSV, updated emergency swap runbook with shadow cutover and audit checklist, and a short decision matrix for dedicated vs hosted fallback by 2027-04-09.
- NexaHealth (Priya/Devon/Tom/Sara) to: run staging replay and validate automation, confirm SSO/audit acceptance, and participate in tabletop on 2027-04-13.
